name: Sapta Vidanga Sthalams — the Seven Dancing Thyagarajas of the Kaveri Delta
theme: Seven temples of Shiva as Thyagaraja in the Somaskanda form, each with an uncarved Vidanga image and its own processional dance, in the Kaveri delta
description: The Sapta Vidanga Sthalams are seven temples of the Kaveri delta where Shiva is worshipped as Thyagaraja in the Somaskanda form — the lord with the Goddess Uma and the child Skanda. In each, the processional Thyagaraja is an uncarved image, a Vidanga ("not chiselled"), said in legend to have been given by the lord to the kings of old; and each Vidanga is held to move in its own distinctive dance when carried in procession. The seven are Thiruvarur, whose Vidhi Vidangar dances the Ajapa Natanam; Nagapattinam, the Nagara Vidangar; Thirukaravasal, the Adhi Vidangar; Thirukkuvalai, the Avani Vidangar; Thiruvaimur, the Nalla Vidangar; Thirunallar, the Sundara Vidangar; and Vedaranyam by the sea, the Bhuvani Vidangar. From Thiruvarur inland to Vedaranyam at the river's mouth, the seven bind the temple towns of the delta into a single pilgrimage of the dancing Thyagaraja.
